success: The exact commit passes local and CI tests and produces deploy evidence.
failureRecovery: A failed build or deploy preserves diagnostics and has a proved recovery path.
rollout: Preview and canary rollout are commit-bound and repeatable.
rollback: Rollback restores the last known-good commit and passes health checks.
telemetry: Build, test, deploy, and rollback results are observable by commit.
customerProof: A pilot user can reach the deployed foundation without manual repair.
operationalProof: CI, deploy, rollback, and evidence receipts agree on one commit.

success: Authorized buyer and seller identities access only their tenant, console, and role.
failureRecovery: Denied, stale, and revoked sessions fail closed and recover through re-authentication.
rollout: Identity and access controls roll out behind commit-bound probes.
rollback: Rollback removes the change without weakening tenant or console isolation.
telemetry: Auth, denial, role, console, and audit events identify the acting tenant and commit.
customerProof: Buyer and seller pilot identities complete allowed actions and are denied forbidden actions.
operationalProof: Isolation, RBAC, audit, security, and recovery probes pass.

success: A buyer creates a workspace and completes phases 1 through 3 in order.
failureRecovery: Invalid gates, stale writes, and failed transitions preserve the last valid state and explain recovery.
rollout: Workspace and evaluation contracts roll out with backward-compatible reads.
rollback: Rollback preserves committed workspace, requirement, and phase data.
telemetry: Workspace, requirement, evaluation, and phase transitions emit correlated events.
customerProof: A buyer pilot completes setup, requirements, use cases, and validation.
operationalProof: State-machine, idempotency, gate, audit, and recovery tests pass.

success: A buyer discovers, invites, confirms, and opens bidding for at least one seller.
failureRecovery: Invitation, confirmation, and bidding-entry failures remain retryable and auditable.
rollout: Invitation and bidding entry roll out to a bounded pilot workspace.
rollback: Rollback stops new entry without losing invitation or shortlist state.
telemetry: Invitation, confirmation, decline, deadline, and bidding-entry events are correlated.
customerProof: A buyer pilot reaches open bidding with the intended seller.
operationalProof: Delivery, retry, audit, gate, and rollback probes pass.

success: An invited seller enters securely, completes onboarding and NDA, authors, and submits a response.
failureRecovery: Expired links, NDA failure, save conflict, and submission failure preserve safe recovery.
rollout: Seller entry and submission roll out to invited pilot sellers only.
rollback: Rollback preserves accepted NDA and submitted response records.
telemetry: Entry, onboarding, NDA, draft, validation, and submission events are correlated.
customerProof: A seller pilot completes the full secure submission path.
operationalProof: Firewall, NDA, draft recovery, submission, audit, and rollback probes pass.

success: The buyer completes phases 7 through 13, reviews, scores, selects, reports, and closes.
failureRecovery: Review, scoring, report, selection, and closure failures preserve the last valid phase and recovery action.
rollout: The remaining journey rolls out to the bounded end-to-end pilot.
rollback: Rollback cannot unlock immutable scores, selections, or terminal closure records.
telemetry: Review, scoring, report, selection, and closure events form one correlated journey.
customerProof: A buyer pilot completes one defensible evaluation and receives its reports.
operationalProof: Phase order, scoring locks, report generation, selection, closure, and recovery probes pass.

success: Closure creates an immutable, exportable, retained, recoverable, access-controlled selection record.
failureRecovery: Export, retention, restore, and access failures fail closed without corrupting the record.
rollout: Record, export, and retention controls roll out after closure proof.
rollback: Rollback preserves immutable records and retention obligations.
telemetry: Record creation, export, retention, restore, denial, and integrity checks are observable.
customerProof: An authorized buyer retrieves and exports the retained selection record.
operationalProof: Immutability, integrity, retention, restore, access, and denial probes pass.

success: The exact commit passes canary, deployed health, and every required runtime gate.
failureRecovery: Canary or runtime failure stops promotion, preserves evidence, and triggers proved recovery.
rollout: Promotion advances only from proved preview to bounded canary to production.
rollback: Production rollback restores the named known-good commit and customer health.
telemetry: Canary, production, gate, incident, rollback, and recovery signals identify the exact commit.
customerProof: The design partner completes the deployed journey on the promoted commit.
operationalProof: Deployment, canary, rollback, runtime-gate, health, and evidence receipts all pass.
